## TL;DR

Repaired the macOS Hub XCTest registry isolation follow-up by using a unique scratch registry, cleaning it up during test-host shutdown, logging cleanup failures, and testing both successful removal and propagated failure. Updated the QA record to preserve the signed-in verification as an explicit human-owned gap. The current review still requires results from held human task #1174 before sign-off.

## Work and rationale

The review found that per-process XCTest scratch directories accumulated. The test host now uses a UUID-named temporary registry directory and removes it from `applicationWillTerminate`. Removal errors are surfaced in the app log instead of being silently ignored. Focused XCTest cases verify directory removal and that a filesystem removal error propagates. The previous focused cleanup test and the final two cleanup tests passed under `xcodebuild` with signing disabled and DerivedData outside the repository.

Merged main to bring the board's updated #1169 specification into the worktree, taking main's copy of the task file per the repository's merge rule. Updated the QA record to point to human task #1174 and to keep signed-in projects and tasks explicitly unverified until that task has results. The current attempt reached the Hub sign-in screen but did not complete authentication.

A later UI launch lacked the disposable registry environment override. The real registry's modification time advanced to 13:19:29 +08. Its contents were not inspected or restored because no before-state was available. The QA record documents the event and clarifies that this launch is not counted as isolated verification.

## Approaches tried

Used a unique per-process temporary directory rather than a PID-derived name, avoiding reuse collisions. Made cleanup throwing so failures can be logged and asserted. Tried inspecting the signed-in flow using the built Hub app; the screen stopped at sign-in, and the launch isolation mistake was recorded rather than claiming the criterion passed.

## Challenges and blockers

Human task #1174 is still waiting for an authorized person to sign in and verify the projects and tasks views on this build. The review requires those observations before sign-off. The email-code automation had not reached those screens. This report does not claim the acceptance criterion is complete.

The focused macOS cleanup XCTest cases passed. The scoped RepoOS check passed earlier in this turn. The required full `repoos check` is being run before this handoff request.

## Key learnings

Test-host scratch data should be unique per process and removed at shutdown, with cleanup failures visible. Launching the native Hub from an automation tool does not inherit the intended QA environment variables; an isolated launch must explicitly set `REPOOS_HUB_SUPPORT_DIRECTORY`. Human authentication checks remain open until the human follow-up records concrete results.
